correctness.rationale: For every observed nonempty sequential anchor ballot, all and only feasible intrinsic rankings are linear extensions of the explicitly constructed rooted tree: necessary constraints follow from running maxima and acceptability, and sufficiency uses either full acceptability or an explicit cutoff just above the best candidate preceding the first retained record. Rooted-tree hook lengths count them, linear-extension orientation of incomparable elements counts the forced pairs, and a reverse-presentation witness proves the no-log comparison. The tolerant expectation, variance, and limiting distribution follow from independent record indicators. Exact exhaustive verifier checks 243 order-record fibers up to seven alternatives and 404 no-log ballots up to five alternatives. Computational tests are corroborative, not an unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The full primary anchoring studies characterize strategic and order-invariant voting outcomes, not the exact tree-poset inverse fiber of hidden rankings, its hook-length count, or the sharp count of additional identified pairwise relations. value.rationale: Collecting the order log is specifically motivated by the source paper as a possible response to presentation bias. The sharp root-tree posterior support and exact reduction of feasible rankings and gain in logically forced pairwise preferences supply a structural identification theorem for actual ranked election data under the specified deterministic mechanism. It quantifies information loss from missing interface metadata and identifies precise limits when voters have unobserved acceptance cutoffs. The result is not a routine output-invariance restatement and does not rely on the classical Dickman law for its novelty.
